### What it does

Improves the fidelity and the error handling of the AIAI/Cleverbase memo signing demonstrator shipped in Release 75.

- **Server** replaces the signed-PDF pipeline. The old path projected the memo through Markdown; the new one goes Yjs → ProseMirror → Tiptap HTML → pdfmake, preserving tables, nested lists, images, underline, links and marks around emoji that the Markdown intermediary dropped. The PDF is the legally-signed artifact, so this changes what a signer actually signs.
- **Client-web** reworks the signing flow's UX: signing-return failures are now surfaced instead of failing silently, signed-copy details are separated from their actions, and signed copies without a signer name get a sensible fallback label.

#### Explicitly verified ABSENT

Recorded because their absence is what makes this release deployable without ceremony:

- **No DB migrations** in either repo — zero files under `src/migrations/`. Nothing to pre-run, nothing to un-run; the migration CronJob is a no-op for this release.
- **No GraphQL schema change.** Server's API surface is byte-identical to 0.165.1 (`Schema Contract` green on the release tip). Client-web's entire generated delta is `+ id` on an existing selection set — and `CalloutContribution.id` is **already in master's own schema snapshot**, so the deployed server already serves it.
- **No authorization change.** No `authorizationPolicyResetAll`, no new privilege, no Kratos/Oathkeeper/session change.
- **No cross-repo deploy ordering constraint.** Client v0.165.1 requires nothing that the currently-deployed server lacks; server needs no client change. Ship in either order.
- **No i18n gap.** 885 keys across all six locales (`en, bg, de, es, fr, nl`), zero missing, zero extra, zero values left identical to English. Two removed keys have no remaining references. No Crowdin round-trip pending.
- **No legacy-MUI drift** — all client-web changes are under `src/crd/*` / `src/main/*`, per the CRD-only convention.
- **Font packaging disproven as a risk.** The single highest-severity theoretical failure (module-scope `fontkit.openSync` throwing at import → server fails to boot) was tested against the **published** `alkemio/server:v0.166.0` image: both `.ttf` files present at the correct `__dirname`-derived paths, `fontkit` present in prod `node_modules`, module loads and routes graphemes correctly inside distroless.
- **Trust-gateway bump (#6487) has zero production impact** — it changes `quickstart-services.yml` and `docs/`, both `.dockerignore`d and never COPYed into the builder. The deployed trust-gateway version is owned by `infrastructure-operations`. It is deliberately **not** listed under Released images.

<details>
  <summary>Perceived Residual Risk</summary>

    - **Overall**: Medium. No migrations, no schema change, no authorization change, and the server's entire source blast radius is one entitlement-gated feature directory — but this ships a complete rewrite of the legally-binding signed artifact under a "patch" label, with a 10x content-budget relaxation on an unthrottled, event-loop-blocking render path, and a client-side change that reaches well outside the signing flow.
    - **Residual Likelihood**: Medium — the fidelity risk needs a real signing walk to retire; the latency tail is already observed, not hypothetical.
    - **Residual Impact**: High in the signed-document case (legal/compliance), Medium elsewhere.
    - **Deploy risk**: Low. No migration, no schema, no auth reset, no data backfill. Rollback is a repin to `server v0.165.1` / `client-web v0.164.1` and is fully reversible in both directions — in-flight signing attempts survive, because `continueMemoSigning` re-reads the **stored** snapshot bytes and compares the **stored** hash rather than re-rendering.
</details>

**Business sign-off: REQUIRED** — specifically for **signed-document fidelity**, not for platform stability. A human must visually accept an ACC-signed PDF containing tables, nested lists, images, underline, links and emoji before PROD promotion. Anyone who signs a memo after this deploy gets a visibly different (intended-better) document than they would have on 0.165.1; changing the signed artifact is a business decision, not an engineering one.

**QA regression sign-off: REQUIRED**, and should not be waived. Scope it to the non-memo blast radius, not the signing flow.

### Release notes

- **Signed PDFs now match what you wrote.** Memos signed through the Cleverbase/AIAI flow preserve tables, nested lists, images, underline, links and formatting around emoji. The previous pipeline routed the memo through Markdown and lost some of this; the signed document is now a faithful rendering of the editor content.
- **Signing failures are visible.** A signing return that fails now surfaces an error instead of failing silently.
- **Clearer signed-copy presentation** — details are separated from their actions, and a signed copy with no signer name shows a sensible fallback label.
- Memos up to ~1 MB of editor content can now be signed (previously ~100 KB of Markdown).
- No change for anyone outside the memo-signing entitlement: the feature remains gated per space and requires a linked Cleverbase identity.

### Downtime & live sessions

*Deploy sequencing is not listed as a task: the pipeline is `validate-inert-artifacts → backup → migrate → deploy`, each gated on the previous, identical in the ACC and PROD workflows. Server and client deploy in the same final job, server first. Nothing to co-ordinate by hand.*

**Live memo and whiteboard collaboration sessions are NOT dropped by this release.**

- `collaboration-service` — the only service whose restart would sever every live session (`strategy: Recreate`, `replicas: 1`) — **stays at `v0.0.3` and is not redeployed**.
- Yjs traffic terminates in `collaboration-service` via `/collab/{documentId}`; Traefik routes it away from `alkemio-server` entirely, so **a server pod restart does not drop collaboration sessions**.
- The signing flow **reuses the already-open websocket** (`requestDurability()` — the same call memo-close already makes). It opens no new socket and no new subscription.
- The server-side memo read joins the room as a **read-only ephemeral participant that produces no awareness or presence** — human editors see no phantom cursor and nothing is evicted.

**Expected downtime on deploy: more than a couple of seconds on the server, brief and pre-existing.**

- `alkemio-server` runs `replicas: 1` with **all three probes commented out** (`11-server-deployment.yml:117/129/141`). With no `readinessProbe` the new pod is marked Ready as soon as the container starts — before NestJS is listening on `:4000` — so traffic is routed into a pod that cannot serve it while the old one is torn down. Expect a **5xx window roughly the length of server bootstrap**.
- **This is pre-existing and not caused by Release 75** (carried from R74; re-verified 09.09). Startup is **not slower** in this release: no `src/core/bootstrap/` changes, `migrationsRun: false` still forces pods never to apply schema at boot, and `TrustGatewayClient`'s constructor makes no network call.
- `client-web` has both liveness and readiness probes and rolls over cleanly.
- **Two ways this release could extend that window** — both covered below: the migration stalling behind a lock (**R-4**) and a PDF render blocking the event loop long enough to trip a liveness probe (**R-5**).

### Trust gateway (new service) — status 09.09 12:30 UTC

**What it is.** `alkemio/trust-gateway` is the Cleverbase signing gateway for memo signing: it holds the Cleverbase client credentials, runs the OAuth service/credential legs, calls `signatures/signHash`, embeds the signature and RFC 3161 timestamp, and answers `POST /v1/verify`. ### Release notes

**Memo signing arrives — sign a memo with your eIDAS identity through Cleverbase.** From a memo, Sign renders its current content into a timestamped PDF server-side, shows you exactly what will be signed, and submits it to Cleverbase; the signed PDF comes back with the signature embedded and is attached to the memo. Signing again adds a new, separately timestamped copy — earlier ones are never replaced. A memo is never itself "signed": it stays a living, editable document, and signatures attach to fixed PDFs capturing a point in time. Signed copies are visible to anyone who can read the memo.

⚠️ **Signing is not operational in this release** — the trust gateway is not deployed, so the Sign button will show an error. Do not announce the feature until the gateway is live.

Also in this release: admin role controls now explain themselves instead of failing after the fact; loading behaviour is calmer across the app (⚠️ the visible word "Loading" no longer appears on full-page loads — intentional, still announced to screen readers); whiteboard drafts older than 7 days are now cleaned up; build reproducibility restored.

### Release notes

**What's new**

- **Delete your own account** — from **User → Security**, behind a typed-name confirmation and a session-freshness check. If your account still owns Spaces, virtual contributors, innovation packs, innovation hubs, or is the sole owner of an organisation, you'll see exactly what's blocking you and where to fix it, with `support@alkem.io` as a parallel route. Deletion is **immediate, permanent and irreversible**. Your profile, settings, files, credentials and sign-in identity are removed; contributions remain but are de-attributed, and **your chat identity is removed by a follow-up rather than instantly**. (`workspace#054`)
- **Search moves into the Space sidebar** — the search and tag filters that used to sit inside the Knowledge Base tab are now a sidebar widget available on **every** tab, with live filtering as you type, toggleable tag chips, and a summary line telling you how many items match. Space admins choose which tabs show it under **Settings → Layout**. (`workspace#055`)
- **Wider, slimmer Space banners** — the default banner shape changes from 6:1 to **10:1** and the minimum width drops from 1536px to 1200px, so more images qualify. Spaces **with** a banner image keep their current shape; Spaces **without** one get the new slimmer header.
- **Promoting a subspace keeps its phases** — moving a subspace up to a top-level Space no longer resets its innovation-flow phases.

**Also changed**

- **The in-content search row is gone.** The Knowledge Base tab no longer has its own search field — the sidebar widget is now the only search entry point. ⚠️ **If an admin has previously emptied a tab's sidebar, that tab will have no search until the Search widget is added back under Settings → Layout.**
- **Post cards no longer show the post-type icon and label**, everywhere they appear.
- The Security settings tab now recovers gracefully when your identity-provider session has lapsed · the emoji picker scrolls properly inside dialogs · contributor cards line up at equal heights · Collabora document export no longer ends your editing session · a long-standing search paging bug (a failed page could permanently stop further loading) is fixed.

> ⚠️ **Wording constraint (R-7):** the deletion flow's step-up check is a **session-freshness** check, **not re-authentication**. Do not describe it as re-authentication in release notes, app-store submissions, or privacy documentation.

### Post-Deployment Steps

- [ ] **Account deletions (`workspace#054`, server#6416) — find and clean up any incompletely-erased account (R-6).**
  **What this is for.** `deleteUser` commits the database deletion in one transaction, then runs the *external* cleanup afterwards as best-effort, un-retried "post-commit legs": deleting the user's file bytes from file-service, removing their Kratos identity, and revoking their sessions. The list of files to delete exists **only in the running pod's memory**. If that pod restarts, is redeployed, or is OOM-killed between the commit and the loop finishing, the user's row is gone but their uploaded file bytes survive — and **no audit row names them**, because the `file_bytes_cleanup_failed` record is only written when the loop actually runs. The result is an **incomplete Art. 17 erasure with nothing pointing at what was left behind**, which is why it has to be looked for rather than reported.
  **Why it is a post-deploy step.** Production runs `replicas: 1`, so the rollout itself is the most likely moment for a deletion to be interrupted mid-flight.
  **Where to monitor — `platform_audit_entry`, NOT the migration logs.** The `migrate` job only covers TypeORM migrations at deploy time; account deletion is a runtime mutation and never appears there. Every deletion writes to `platform_audit_entry` with `category = 'account_deletion'`, grouped by `"subjectUserId"` (note: **quoted camelCase** columns, and `correlationId` is *not* populated by this path). A complete deletion leaves **four** rows: the primary `account_deleted` plus one terminal outcome per leg —
  `identity_deletion_completed` / `identity_deletion_failed` · `file_bytes_cleanup_completed` / `file_bytes_cleanup_failed` · `session_revocation_completed` / `session_invalidation_failed`.

  That gives three distinguishable states, and **the audit table detects all three**:

  | state | signature | meaning |
  |---|---|---|
  | ✅ complete | primary + all three terminal rows | fully erased |
  | ⚠️ leg failed | primary + a `*_failed` row | **self-describing** — `failureReason` and `details` name what failed |
  | 🚨 **stranded** | primary + **missing** terminal rows | the pod died between commit and legs; **nothing names what was left behind** |

  **Run this after the deploy** — it finds the stranded case, which is the one nothing else reports:
  ```sql
  SELECT a."subjectUserId", min(a."createdDate") AS deleted_at,
         bool_or(a.outcome = 'identity_deletion_completed')  AS identity_ok,
         bool_or(a.outcome = 'file_bytes_cleanup_completed') AS files_ok,
         bool_or(a.outcome = 'session_revocation_completed') AS sessions_ok
  FROM platform_audit_entry a
  WHERE a.category = 'account_deletion'
    AND a."createdDate" >= now() - interval '7 days'
  GROUP BY a."subjectUserId"
  HAVING bool_or(a.outcome = 'account_deleted')
     AND NOT (bool_or(a.outcome IN ('identity_deletion_completed','identity_deletion_failed'))
          AND bool_or(a.outcome IN ('file_bytes_cleanup_completed','file_bytes_cleanup_failed'))
          AND bool_or(a.outcome IN ('session_revocation_completed','session_invalidation_failed')))
  ORDER BY deleted_at DESC;
  ```
  *(Supported by `ix_platform_audit_entry_subject_category_created`.)* **Zero rows = nothing stranded, and this item is done.**

### Do we need an authorization reset? — **NO global reset required** (verified 01.09 against `release/73`)

**Answer: no `authorizationPolicyResetAll`, and no manual reset step.** Verified directly against the final release branch, not the original scope.

**What changed in authorization, and why none of it needs existing data recomputed:**

| change | affects existing entities? | why |
|---|---|---|
| **New `MOVE_TASK` privilege** (the only new privilege in the release) | **No** | Appended *only* when `isTaskBoard(callout)`. A Tasks board requires the new `callout_contribution.classificationId` column plus a reserved `task` classification tagset — **it cannot exist before this release**. Existing callouts neither gain nor need it; new boards get it at creation. `MOVE_CONTRIBUTION` and every other move privilege are untouched. |
| **Contribution → classification cascade** | **No** | Guarded by `if (contribution.classification)`. The column is new, nullable, and **not backfilled**, so every pre-existing contribution is `NULL` and there is nothing to cascade into. |
| **`ClassificationEntry`** (Space Classifications) | **No** | Carries **no authorization policy of its own**; all six mutations gate on `UPDATE` of the owning `SpaceAbout`. |
| **StorageBucket cascade guard** | **No** | Adds a `continue` for NULL-authz documents. Skips work; computes nothing new. |
| **Template `CLASSIFICATION` case** | **No** | Adds a `break` to a switch. No policy computed for that type. |

**Three caveats that do matter operationally:**

1. **A scoped authorization reset runs automatically on first boot — you do not trigger it, and you cannot skip it.** `ensureClassificationTemplatesArePresent()` seeds the platform Classification pack and then calls `accountAuthorizationService.applyAuthorizationPolicy()` on the host account, recursing through every space, subspace, callout, VC and pack it owns. It runs **before `app.listen()`**. This is **R-3**, and it is the single largest unmeasured risk in the release — see the pre-deployment steps.

2. **After this release, an authorization reset REQUIRES the new server code.** Two guards were added precisely because a reset would otherwise **throw**:
   - `TemplateAuthorizationService` — on `master` the `default:` branch throws `EntityNotFoundException("Unable to reset auth on template of type: …")`. Bootstrap **seeds a Classification Template**, so on old code any subsequent reset dies on it.
   - `DocumentAuthorizationService` — on `master`, `if (!document.tagset || !document.tagset.authorization) throw new RelationshipNotFoundException(...)`. Collaboration writes NULL-authz Yjs snapshot documents into storage buckets, so on old code any subsequent reset dies on them.

   **Consequence for rollback:** rolling the server back to `v0.162.0` while keeping Release 73 data leaves the platform in a state where **authorization resets throw**. Routine auth-reset operations would fail until the server is rolled forward again. Combined with the roll-forward-only migration (R-5), a server rollback is not a clean escape hatch.

3. **If anyone runs a full reset post-deploy**, it will traverse classification templates and collaboration snapshot documents for the first time. That path is newly exercised — safe on `v0.163.4`, untested at scale.

### Pre-Deployment Steps

Run **per environment**, in this order. Acceptance and production are independent runs.

**A. Before the deploy starts**

- [ ] **Verified DB backup taken.** This release is **roll-forward only** — `AddSpaceClassifications` is non-idempotent with a destructive `down()` (R-5), and a server rollback additionally breaks authorization resets (see the authorization section). The backup is the only true escape hatch.
- [ ] **Coordinated DB + file-storage backup** for the collaboration cutover specifically (R-24).
- [ ] **Time the migration transaction on ACC-sized data.** Nine migrations run in **one transaction** (`migrationsTransactionMode` unset → default `all`), so the `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock from the `callout_contribution` UNIQUE index build and the full `user_settings` jsonb rewrite are held until the last one commits (R-4, R-6). **Unmeasured today.**
- [ ] **Measure first-pod `bootstrap()` wall-clock on ACC.** Production is `replicas: 1` with **all three probes commented out**, so K8s marks the pod Ready the moment the container starts and routes traffic to it while bootstrap is still running before `app.listen()`. **The outage window equals bootstrap duration and nobody has measured it** (R-3).

### Release notes

**What's new**
- **Unified memo and whiteboard collaboration** — both editors now use one Yjs collaboration service and one canonical snapshot per document in its own file-storage bucket. Existing documents are progressively unlocked by separate idempotent memo/whiteboard migration operations; embedded media is up-homed and verified. (`workspace#006`, #1909)
- **Kanban Task Boards** — a Posts callout can now be a **Tasks board**: ordered columns, task cards with per-column counters, drag-and-drop moves, column management (create, rename, reorder, delete), a fullscreen board view, and template round-trip. Moving a task is member-executable. (`workspace#042`)
- **Space Classifications** — structured, reusable **Classifications** (starting with the SDGs) alongside freeform Tags. Add one from a template, pick its values, show or hide it on the Space About page, and author your own Classification templates in the Templates manager. (`workspace#024`)
- **Connected Accounts** — connect, use and disconnect your sign-in methods (including **Cleverbase**) from **User → Security**, with your password and passkeys shown alongside, and a guard that stops you removing your only way in. (`workspace#051`)
- **Reaction notifications** — get notified when someone reacts to your Post, by in-app, push and email, with a per-type setting under User → Notifications. Email is **off by default** (opt-in). (`workspace#041`)
- **A refreshed Space page** — a sticky tab bar that stays with you as you scroll, restyled tabs and banner, relocated header actions, stacked subspace cards, breadcrumb avatars, and an edge-swipe drawer on mobile. The refresh also lightens the background across the whole app.

- **Configurable Space sidebar** — Space admins can choose which widgets appear in the sidebar, per tab, from Settings ▸ Layout, with drag-to-reorder and a new permission-gated **Add Post** button. (`workspace#040`)

**Fixes / polish:** whiteboard templates can be drawn on again while being created; moving a contribution into, out of or between task boards now keeps its column classification correct; LinkedIn profile avatars are picked up on social sign-up again; a new subspace shows up immediately with its avatar and banner; "Show all" on Subspaces opens the dialog rather than jumping to a tab; emoji reactions are hidden where comments are turned off; joining-member notifications show the right avatar; the markdown table menu no longer hides behind dialogs; the whiteboard editor dialog is properly labelled for screen readers; cold sign-in no longer dead-ends when a login flow is rejected (with a recovery card and a proper lockout screen); creating a Space from a template with any number of flow phases now works; "X applied to join" notifications open Settings ▸ Community where you can act on them; no more spurious error toast when deleting a template; Dutch reactions copy, "Post" capitalization, and Innovation Pack visibility labels corrected.

**Note on the version numbers.** This ships a *feature* under a *patch* bump, because 71.1 is a patch on the release-71 line rather than the next release. `0.161.1 → 0.161.2` understates the change: it adds a new self-service credential surface, a GraphQL surface, and a migration. ### What it does

Gives MCP API keys a lifecycle surface — mint, list, revoke — in user Security settings, plus an API-only admin surface for support/offboarding, with audit rows for every mint and revoke.

**It also closes two live security defects found while building it.** Neither was in the story text; both blocked its acceptance criteria as written:

1. **Key-chaining privilege escalation.** `/rest/mcp/api-keys` carried POST/GET/DELETE handlers behind the same guard that accepts MCP API keys, so a leaked key could mint replacement keys — uncapped, unaudited. Internet-reachable in production and acceptance via `PathPrefix(/rest/mcp)`. Revoking a leaked key did not end the compromise. All three handlers deleted.
2. **Revocation did not take effect until the transport closed.** An established MCP session only ever upgraded its identity, so a revoked key kept full authority until the pod restarted. Sessions now revalidate on the branch that did not authenticate afresh — the normal key-bearing path adds no extra reads.

**Platform (server + client-web)**
- **Redesigned home dashboard** — a non-activity home view with a per-user toggle and space activity scoring (`workspace#024`).

- **Resilience** — a Redis outage now *degrades* auth (503 + Retry-After) instead of rejecting all traffic or killing the process (specs 108/109); a null user profile can no longer crash the server. **Privacy** — account deletion revokes OIDC/BFF + Kratos sessions (GDPR Art. 17).

## Important findings captured

1. Restore wrappers must propagate failures; Job creation/completion alone is not proof of a valid restore.
2. ChromaDB must be restored into its offline PVC.
3. PostgreSQL globals, replication roles, slots and target-local certificates must be bootstrapped explicitly; standby storage is disposable and reseeded after primary restore.
4. NFS `All_Squash` identity must align with file-service UID/GID `65532`; bulk restore is safest through the stopped Ganesha backing volume.
5. Deployment automation must generate and fence a target-specific IAM kubeconfig.
6. Runtime rendering must explicitly own lifecycle fields: omitting `spec.suspend` does not clear a value previously applied by the dark overlay.
7. DNS cutover is the decisive end-to-end validation, but login/Hydra and application services may require restart after the DNS TTL expires.
8. Dynamically provisioned Scaleway PVCs must omit `spec.selector`; even `selector: {}` is rejected by Scaleway CSI.
9. Prometheus/Alertmanager and the independent external dead-man heartbeat are separate failure domains; acceptance still needs its own external heartbeat endpoint.
10. cert-manager requires explicit RBAC for the Scaleway ACME challenge resource. Both clusters currently serve valid certificates, but renewal is blocked until this is corrected.

  - Orphan hygiene: after the last reference is dropped and the blob deleted, still-pending hints for that hash are removed, guarded by the live `file` table so a concurrent re-upload does not lose its new hint.
  - Moves legacy image-dimension repair out of the request path into the explicit keyset-paged `sweep-dims` subcommand + a fail-closed manual Job manifest.

#### file-backup-service (`v0.0.4 → v0.0.5`) — released [2026-07-23](https://github.com/alkem-io/file-backup-service/releases/tag/v0.0.5), **not yet deployed to any environment**
- **alkem-io/file-backup-service#6 — fix(008): fetch source bytes by content hash, not by document id**
  - **Bug fixed (observed live on Acceptance).** The worker fetched `GET /internal/file/{id}/content` — by *mutable document id* — then verified the stream against the enqueued hash. For anything whose content changed between enqueue and backup (**every Collabora document**: created empty, then filled; plus any edited file) file-service returned the *current* bytes, which hash to something ≠ the enqueued hash:
    ```
    backup failed: integrity: stream hash 828448d2… != a7ffc6f8…   (a7ffc6f8 = SHA3-256 of empty)
    ```
    Those dead-lettered. **Not data loss** — the real content was backed up via its own outbox row — but it burned the dead-letter budget, and any version superseded before the worker read it was simply unfetchable (by-id only ever returns current; the old blob is refcount-deleted).
  - **Fix.** `FetchContent` now GETs `/internal/blob/{hash}/content` keyed by `ExternalID`. A blob under a hash is immutable, so the fetch is **version-exact**: it returns the exact enqueued bytes, or a clean 404 → `ErrSourceGone` (a superseded, GC'd version — recorded *skipped*, not *failed*). A content-addressed fetch cannot return the wrong bytes, so the integrity check can no longer false-fire.
  - `Preflight` is now **strict**: it probes a valid never-existing hash, proving the `/blob` route is reachable, and **fails loud on deploy skew** rather than starting against a file-service that lacks the endpoint.
- No DB migration. Worker/CLI only — no user-facing surface.

### Production prerequisite — the immutable S3 target is NOT the acceptance one (008)

> **Not in this release's deployable scope.** Production continuous backup stays draft-gated: the worker's base reference remains commented out in `overlays/production/kustomization.yml`. This section records what must be provisioned **before** that gate can ever be opened, because the work is out-of-band and needs a human — nothing in a deploy pipeline creates it.

Acceptance and production do **not** share a backup target. Production requires an **independent, immutable** bucket (FR-014 / SC-006): if losing the production cluster or its Scaleway account could also destroy the backups, it is not a backup.

#### 1. Provision the bucket out-of-band (Scaleway)

| Property | Required value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Account / project | **Separate** from the primary cluster's | Independent failure domain — losing the prod account must not touch the backups |
| Region | **`fr-par`** (primary is `nl-ams`) | Geographic independence |
| Object Lock | **COMPLIANCE mode, default retention 30 days** | Not even the account root can delete or overwrite within retention |
| Versioning | **Enabled** | Required by Object Lock; also guards against overwrite |
| SSE | **Enabled** (provider-managed) | Encryption at rest |
| `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` lifecycle | **1–7 days** | **Not optional.** Streamed unknown-length uploads force multipart; a mid-stream abort is 403'd by the write-only credential and orphans the multipart, so the bucket must reap them itself |
| Worker credential | **PutObject-only, no delete** | The worker must have no delete path to a backup |

#### 2. Environment variables that differ for production

Only three keys are overridden per environment; the rest are inherited from the base ConfigMap. One key is **production-only**.

| Variable | Where set | Acceptance | **Production** |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FBS_TARGET_OFFSITE_ENDPOINT` | overlay | `s3.nl-ams.scw.cloud` | **`s3.fr-par.scw.cloud`** |
| `FBS_TARGET_OFFSITE_REGION` | overlay | `nl-ams` | **`fr-par`** |
| `FBS_TARGET_OFFSITE_BUCKET` | overlay | `alkemio-s3-test-replication` | **`alkemio-file-backup-prod-immutable`** |
| `FBS_TARGET_OFFSITE_WORM` | prod overlay **only** | _(unset)_ | **`true`** |
| `FBS_TARGETS` | base | `offsite` | inherited |
| `FBS_TARGET_OFFSITE_TYPE` | base | `s3` | inherited |
| `FBS_TARGET_OFFSITE_USESSL` | base | `true` | inherited (TLS in transit, required) |
| `FBS_TARGET_OFFSITE_SSE` | base | `true` | inherited (encryption at rest, required) |

`FBS_TARGET_OFFSITE_WORM=true` is what tells the worker and the audit job to **expect read/`Exists` to be denied** — with a PutObject-only credential those calls legitimately fail, and without this flag they would be read as target errors.

#### ⚠️ Exactly three variables change for production — set them explicitly

All three already carry their **declared** values in
`orchestration/overlays/production/alkemio/collaboration-platform/backend/file-backup-service/12-file-backup-service-config.yml`.
Those are the *intent*, not a confirmed fact — the bucket does not exist yet. **Whoever provisions the
target must reconcile these three against what was actually created.** A bucket in another region, or
under another name, backs nothing up while every job still reports success.

| # | Variable | Currently declared | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `FBS_TARGET_OFFSITE_ENDPOINT` | `s3.fr-par.scw.cloud` | Set to the endpoint of the region the bucket was actually created in |
| 2 | `FBS_TARGET_OFFSITE_REGION` | `fr-par` | Must match #1, and must **not** be the primary's `nl-ams` — a same-region target defeats the geographic independence this target exists for |
| 3 | `FBS_TARGET_OFFSITE_BUCKET` | `alkemio-file-backup-prod-immutable` | Set to the real bucket name |

Everything else (`FBS_TARGETS`, `FBS_TARGET_OFFSITE_TYPE`, `_USESSL`, `_SSE`) is inherited from the
base ConfigMap and must **not** be restated in the production overlay.

Verify after editing, before the promotion PR is opened:

```bash
kustomize build orchestration/overlays/production \
  | grep -A12 'name: alkemio-file-backup-service-config'
```

The rendered ConfigMap must show all three production values, and `nl-ams` must appear nowhere in it.

#### ⚠️ 3. Two secrets must be replaced with the real production credential

Both are checked in as **placeholders that decode to `REPLACE_ME_prod_*`**, so a forgotten override fails
closed rather than silently reusing an acceptance credential. They must end up holding the **actual
production values** before the promotion PR is opened.

File: `orchestration/overlays/production/alkemio/collaboration-platform/backend/file-backup-service/13-file-backup-service-secrets.yml`

| Secret key | Currently decodes to | Must become |
|---|---|---|
| `FBS_TARGET_OFFSITE_ACCESSKEY` | `REPLACE_ME_prod_offsite_access_key` | The real access key of the **PutObject-only / no-delete (WORM)** credential on the separate immutable account |
| `FBS_TARGET_OFFSITE_SECRETKEY` | `REPLACE_ME_prod_offsite_secret_key` | Its secret half |

Values go under `data:` and must be **base64-encoded** (repo convention — a raw string there fails at
runtime, not at apply time):

```bash
printf '%s' '<real-access-key>' | base64
printf '%s' '<real-secret-key>' | base64
```

**The credential itself is the requirement, not just its presence.** Quoting the manifest header
(SC-006 / FR-014 / FR-028): it *"MUST be a Scaleway credential scoped PutObject-ONLY / NO-DELETE
(WORM) on the separate immutable account — the worker must have no delete/overwrite path to the
immutable backup. Object-lock (compliance, 30d) is the belt; the write-only credential is the
braces."* A credential with delete rights would satisfy every check here and still defeat the
purpose of the target.

Verify nothing was missed before promoting:

```bash
kustomize build orchestration/overlays/production \
  | grep -A8 'name: alkemio-file-backup-secrets' \
  | grep -o 'UkVQTEFDRV9NRV9wcm9k[A-Za-z0-9+/=]*' \
  && echo "STILL PLACEHOLDERS — do not promote"
```

(`FBS_ALKEMIODB_PASSWORD` and `FBS_LEDGERDB_PASSWORD` in the same file are likewise prod-specific
placeholders needing real values, but they are database credentials rather than S3 — the DB roles
must exist first.)

#### 4. Activation order — one promotion PR, never a direct-to-main PR

1. Provision the bucket per §1 and inject the §3 credentials.
2. **Validate WORM delete-rejection** with the worker credential, plus a restore drill.
3. Uncomment the base reference in `overlays/production/kustomization.yml` and its two patches.
4. Flip the file-service producer on for production (`FILE_BACKUP_OUTBOX_ENABLED=true`) **last**, so no outbox rows accrue before there is a worker to drain them.

### Release notes
- **Reliable backups for collaborative documents.** The continuous file-backup worker now fetches source bytes **by content hash** instead of by document id, so it always captures the exact version that was queued. Previously any file whose content changed between being queued and being backed up — which is **every Collabora document**, since they are created empty and then filled — failed an integrity check and landed in the dead-letter queue. No data was ever lost (the real content was queued separately), but the failures were noisy and any superseded version could not be re-fetched. Backups of edited and collaborative documents now complete cleanly, and a version that has genuinely been superseded is recorded as *skipped* rather than *failed*.
- **Safer, lower-memory file serving.** file-service now streams every file and blob response end to end with correct `Content-Length`, detects truncated or faulty backend reads, and distinguishes a client hanging up from a real storage failure. Large-file reads no longer scale memory with concurrency.
- **A backup gap closed.** Documents promoted from temporary to permanent storage now correctly enter the backup queue; previously such a document could stay permanently outside the backup window.
- **Housekeeping.** Stale backup hints are cleaned up when the last reference to a file is deleted, and legacy image-dimension repair moved out of the request path into an explicit maintenance job.

### Release notes

Release 69 lands the **Platform Operations Admin role** (`workspace#032`) — a least-privilege seat for routine platform upkeep (authorization/license resets, search & AI re-index, embeddings cleanup & VC knowledge refresh, avatar/whiteboard migrations, notification prune, comms housekeeping, geolocation refresh), so operators no longer need full global admin to run maintenance. Every operational action is audit-logged. It also adds **moving an L2 subspace to an L1 parent under a different top-level space** (`workspace#030`) from Platform Administration → Conversions & Transfers, with a searchable destination picker; moving a subspace clears its community roles and pending invitations (the confirmation names these consequences). A **privacy fix** (`server#6304`) ensures cross-L0 subspace moves recompute platform-role access so a public subspace moved into a private space no longer keeps public visibility. Smaller improvements: non-admin creators can reach the **organization create form**, signed-in visitors correctly **land on hub home** on innovation-hub subdomains, the **cookie banner** is dismissed once across subdomains, plus a `file.externalID` **hot-path index** and a shared **CI-runner migration** (`workspace#027`). This is a **coordinated, server-first** release: the Ops-Admin and Move-subspaces UIs need their paired server version live first, and a **one-time platform authorization reset must run post-deploy** for the new operational privilege to take effect.

### Release notes

Release 68 lands **callout manual selection** (`workspace#025`) — Contributors and Subspaces collection callouts can now be curated with an explicit `CUSTOM` selection alongside the existing `AUTO` mode — and **OfficeDocs disconnect-during-edit recovery** (`workspace#015`, deferred from R67), which detects a lost connection to the Collabora save service and guides the user to recover their edit. It also fixes **whole-day calendar events** to display and export on the correct date regardless of timezone (`workspace#023`), makes the **login indicator derive from the OIDC BFF session** so the header no longer shows "logged out" while the session is still valid, and adds smaller UX fixes: **close/reopen polls**, correct **emoji insertion** next to mentions, **post-index phase sorting**, a **footer logo**, and **hiding inactive spaces** on organization profiles. **notifications** fixes **email subject escaping** (special characters like `&` now render correctly), removes its unused Apollo dependency, and bumps `notifications-lib` to 0.18.0. This is a **coordinated, server-first** release: the callout-selection and Collabora-recovery slices need their paired server version live first, and the Collabora `accessTokenTTL` value changed meaning (now an absolute expiry timestamp) — deploy server before client.

### Release notes

Release 67 lands **Collabora office-document search** (`workspace#009`) — office-document content is now indexed and surfaced in search results — plus **rename and replace-in-place** for callout Collabora documents (spec 114). It adds two new cross-repo features: **notification sounds** with an unread-tab badge and per-user sound settings (`workspace#020`), and **flow-state post-layout settings** (`workspace#021`). Under the hood, both server and client-web complete the **TypeScript 7 (native tsgo) build-toolchain upgrade** (`workspace#019`), server adds the (dormant) **file-backup outbox** table and **file-service** ships the flag-gated producer (`workspace#008`) — **staged only; the backup flow is not switched on in R67 and its consumer lands in a later release** — enables **subspace direct-join** for non-members of the parent community, and makes **OIDC login resilient** (the server no longer crash-loops when the identity issuer is briefly unreachable). Also: **calendar fixes** (event date validation + whole-day handling client-side, and a whole-day export date fix server-side), a **sign-in tagline** update with new translations, a **PWA icon/branding revamp**, and whiteboard-escape and callout/map UX refinements. **notifications** corrects the comment-notification email copy ("your post" → "the post", alkem-io/notifications#549 closing alkem-io/notifications#548) and completes its own TS7 upgrade. This is a **coordinated, server-first release**: the Collabora, #020-sounds, and #021-flow-state slices need their paired server versions, the #020 settings migration must run before its resolver, wopi-service v0.1.3 must lead server, and the TS7 swap requires a real production build/boot smoke test before promotion.

#### Perceived Residual Risk

**Medium.** No release category is High overall. The elevated areas (DB schema, GraphQL contract, auth logic, infra/manifests) are all **clean** — the three server migrations (`BackfillL0InnovationFlowMaxStates`, `BackfillUserSettingsAllowContactViaEmail`, `AddIcsMimeType`) are all idempotent jsonb **data backfills with no DDL/schema change**, and the GraphQL changes (u2u messaging, .ics enum, scoped-search inputs) are **purely additive**. The combined rating is pulled to Medium solely by the **blast radius of the full MUI/Emotion removal** in client-web: a large app-wide refactor where a miss surfaces as a visual/UX regression (not data loss) and is reversible by redeploying the prior client image. The newly added features (u2u messaging, KB scoped search, Collabora activity tracking, .ics) are additive and individually low-residual.

**Business sign-off:** _not required_ on contract grounds (no repo is High). **Design/QA visual sign-off is warranted** given the MUI removal. Note the **opt-in `allowContactViaEmail`** default (`false`) for the new messaging path — confirm the privacy default with the product owner.

### Risk Profile

> ⚠️ **Overall risk: HIGH — business sign-off required.** Both `server` and `client-web` are rated HIGH independently. This release rewrites the platform-wide authentication path with **no feature flag and no fallback** on either side; a misordered or misconfigured deploy logs out 100% of users. It also introduces a **breaking inter-service IPC change** that mandates a coordinated lockstep deploy. Requires staged rollout (staging-first), login/logout smoke tests on the target infra, and a tested rollback to 0.150.0.

### Pre-Deployment Tasks
Migration follows the [synapse-migrator two-phase workflow](https://github.com/alkem-io/synapse-migrator#3-two-phase-migration-workflow):

- [x] 1. Stop Matrix/Synapse deployments on acceptance
- [x] 2. Disable communications (`COMMUNICATIONS_ENABLED=false` on alkemio-server)
- [x] 3. Create full backup of Synapse and Alkemio databases
- [x] 4. Restore backups to local environment
- [x] 5. Run pre-shutdown phase locally: `migrate --phase=pre-shutdown --dry-run` then execute
- [x] 6. Stop Synapse locally
- [x] 7. Run post-shutdown phase locally: `migrate --phase=post-shutdown`
- [x] 8. Create backups from migrated local databases
- [x] 9. Upload migrated backups to Scaleway Object Storage
- [x] 10. Use built-in restore mechanism to restore migrated backups to acceptance
- [x] 11. Restart Matrix/Synapse deployments
- [x] 12. Re-enable communications (`COMMUNICATIONS_ENABLED=true`)
- [x] Config regarding the AI service is applied as part of the deployment
